facts.text: The nine levels of control are the mining industry's defenses against vehicle interactions, ranging from site design at Level 1 to automatic machine braking at Level 9, with warning technology at Levels 7 and 8.
facts.quote: The nine levels of control are the mining industry's ladder of defenses against vehicle interactions, running from how a site is designed (Level 1) to a machine that brakes by itself (Level 9), with warning technology at Levels 7 and 8.

facts.text: The nine-level control model comes from EMESRT (Earth Moving Equipment Safety Round Table), a group of mining companies, through its performance requirement PR-5A.
facts.quote: The model comes from EMESRT (the Earth Moving Equipment Safety Round Table), a group of mining companies, in its performance requirement PR-5A

facts.text: ICMM (International Council on Mining and Metals), regulators and suppliers worldwide use the nine-level control model.
facts.quote: it is used by the ICMM (International Council on Mining and Metals), regulators and suppliers worldwide [Chapters 1, 3, 5]

facts.text: Level 1 of the nine-level control model is site requirements: the layout and rules of the site itself.
facts.quote: Site requirements: the layout and rules of the site itself.

facts.text: Level 2 of the nine-level control model is segregation controls: keeping people, light vehicles and heavy machines apart.
facts.quote: Segregation controls: keeping people, light vehicles and heavy machines apart.

facts.text: Level 3 of the nine-level control model is operating procedures: written rules for how work is done.
facts.quote: Operating procedures: the written rules for how work is done.

facts.text: Level 4 of the nine-level control model is authority to operate: who may drive which machines.
facts.quote: Authority to operate: who may drive what.

facts.text: Level 5 of the nine-level control model is fitness to operate, covering fatigue, health and impairment.
facts.quote: Fitness to operate: fatigue, health, impairment.

facts.text: Level 6 of the nine-level control model is operating compliance: whether the rules are actually followed.
facts.quote: Operating compliance: whether the rules are actually followed.

facts.text: Level 7 of the nine-level control model is operator awareness: technology that helps operators see and know, such as cameras and proximity displays.
facts.quote: Operator awareness: technology that helps the operator see and know, such as cameras and proximity displays.

facts.text: Level 8 of the nine-level control model is advisory controls: technology that advises the operator to act.
facts.quote: Advisory controls: technology that advises the operator to act.

facts.text: Level 9 of the nine-level control model is intervention controls: technology that acts on the machine by slowing and stopping it.
facts.quote: Intervention controls: technology that acts on the machine, slowing and stopping it.

facts.text: Levels 1 to 6 of the nine-level control model concern people, places and procedures; Levels 7 to 9 concern technology progressing through awareness, advice and action.
facts.quote: Levels 1 to 6 are about people, places and procedures. Levels 7 to 9 are technology and form a ladder of their own: awareness, advice, action.

facts.text: The manufacturer's existing proximity warning operates at Levels 7 and 8 of the nine-level control model.
facts.quote: The manufacturer's existing proximity warning sits at Levels 7 and 8

facts.text: The Collision Mitigation System is a Level 9 control in the nine-level control model.
facts.quote: the Collision Mitigation System is a Level 9 control.

facts.text: ICMM and EMESRT state that effective implementation of Level 8 and 9 controls requires first understanding the effectiveness of the Level 1 to 7 baseline during normal operations; higher-level controls do not replace the lower levels.
facts.quote: ICMM and EMESRT state that implementing Level 8 and 9 controls well requires first understanding the effectiveness of the Level 1 to 7 baseline for normal operations, and that "there are no silver bullets" [Chapter 1].

facts.text: Regulatory emphasis differs: New South Wales and NIOSH favor lower-level controls with Levels 7 to 9 as backup, whereas South Africa has legally required Level 9 intervention since December 2022.
facts.quote: Regulators differ in emphasis: New South Wales and NIOSH favor the lower levels with Levels 7 to 9 as backup, while South Africa has made Level 9 intervention a legal requirement since December 2022 [Chapter 4].

facts.text: The Australian ACARP test framework uses two tiers: prove object detection first, then prove Level 8 or 9 intervention.
facts.quote: The Australian ACARP test framework follows the same logic in two tiers: prove object detection first, then Level 8 or 9 intervention [Chapter 1].

facts.text: The same braking algorithm can be safe at one site and troublesome at another because the site's Level 1 to 6 controls determine how often people and machines legitimately get close.
facts.quote: the same braking algorithm can be safe at one site and troublesome at another: the site's own Level 1 to 6 controls decide how often people and machines legitimately get close [Chapter 1].

facts.text: Epiroc describes staged release as running its system on site without immediately enforcing Level 9 intervention; the nine-level control model supplies the program's staged-release vocabulary.
facts.quote: They also give the plan its vocabulary for staged release, which is how Epiroc describes running its system on site "without immediately enforcing level-9 intervention" [Chapter 1].
